turns.question: I'm thinking of retiring at 58. Am I eligible, and how much would I get?
turns.answer:
At age 58, you appear to meet the Article 11 service requirement for the retirement formula because you have 21.5 years of service. Section 11-134 permits an employee with at least 20 years of service to begin an annuity before age 60, but it applies a reduction of 0.25% for each month the annuity begins before age 60. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

The estimate is **$36,567.41 per year**, or **$3,047.28 per month**, beginning at age 58.

**What I assumed:** the date you stop working is taken as today. The calculation also reflects continuous employment until that date and the salary basis used for the estimate.

The early-retirement provisions in Sections 11-133.1 and 11-133.2 do not reach your planned retirement because they required applications and withdrawals during specified periods in 1992–1993 or 1997–1998. Section 11-133.3 also concerns a specified 2003–2004 retirement window. [40 ILCS 5/11-133.1] [40 ILCS 5/11-133.2] [40 ILCS 5/11-133.3]

I’m going by your record, which places you in Article 11 — tell me if that’s not right. I could not establish from the sections available whether another Article 11 retirement provision or an election would produce a different amount.

This is an estimate — your retirement fund makes the binding determination.

turns.question: what does Article 4 provide for police officers?
turns.answer:
Article 4 provides pension benefits for municipal **firefighters**, not police officers. It creates and administers firefighters’ pension funds in qualifying municipalities, including certain fire protection districts. [40 ILCS 5/4-101] [40 ILCS 5/4-103]

It defines a covered firefighter as certain fire-service employees whose duties include controlling and extinguishing fires. [40 ILCS 5/4-106] The Article provides:

- Retirement pensions, including rules for firefighters with at least 20 years of creditable service and separate provisions for people who first became firefighters on or after January 1, 2011. [40 ILCS 5/4-109]
- Disability pensions for disabilities resulting from an act of duty or from other causes. [40 ILCS 5/4-110] [40 ILCS 5/4-111]
- Medical review and restoration-to-service procedures for disability pensions. [40 ILCS 5/4-112]
- Survivor pensions. [40 ILCS 5/4-114]
- Refunds of contributions for certain firefighters with less than 20 years of service who leave employment. [40 ILCS 5/4-116]

The text reviewed does not establish that Article 4 applies to police officers, and it does not establish the rules for your Article 11 pension. I'm going by your record, which places you in Article 11 — tell me if that's not right.
